# Bondi

> Bondi is a Mac app that tells you why your Mac is slow in one plain sentence, written on the Mac by Apple's on-device model. It's made by Jabble Super Intelligence Inc.

- Status: the beta is launching soon, and the full launch follows it. Bondi can't be bought yet.
- What it does: groups every running process under the app that started it, finds what's holding memory, warns about one cause at a time and asks before it quits or stops anything, and keeps 30 days of history on the Mac.
- AI: runs on the Mac. On Macs with Apple Intelligence (macOS 26, Apple silicon) it uses Apple's on-device foundation model. Other Macs can download a small open model (Qwen2.5 0.5B) from Settings. Bondi computes every number itself, and the AI only writes the words around them.
- Data: history stays in a file on the Mac. The app contacts Jabble's server only to check its trial or license and to look for updates. There's no account and no analytics.
- Requirements: macOS 15 or later, on Apple silicon or Intel.
- Pricing at full launch: a 7-day free trial, then a one-time purchase for one Mac, with no subscription. The first 250 licenses cost $6.99, and after that the price is $29.99. Paddle is the merchant of record. Refunds are available within 14 days.

## Blog
- [Why is my Mac slow? How to find the real cause](https://trybondi.app/blog/why-is-my-mac-slow.md): Mac running slow? It usually comes down to one of a handful of causes. Here's how to tell which one it is, with real readings from a real MacBook Pro.
- [Which app is using my Mac's memory?](https://trybondi.app/blog/which-app-is-using-my-mac-memory.md): Apps like Chrome split into dozens of helper processes, so Activity Monitor hides the real total. Here's how to see which app is really using your Mac's memory.
- [Memory pressure on Mac, explained](https://trybondi.app/blog/memory-pressure-explained.md): "Memory Used" being high is normal on a Mac. Memory pressure, swap and compressed memory tell you whether you actually need more. Here's how to read them.
- [Why are my Mac's fans so loud?](https://trybondi.app/blog/mac-fans-loud.md): Loud fans on a MacBook or any Mac mean the chip is working hard or running hot. Here's how to find what's heating it, and what to do if they won't settle.
- [kernel_task using lots of CPU? Your Mac is cooling itself down](https://trybondi.app/blog/kernel-task-high-cpu.md): kernel_task at high CPU usually means your Mac is hot, and macOS is slowing apps on purpose to cool it. Here's why it happens and what actually helps.
- [WindowServer using high CPU on Mac: what it means and what helps](https://trybondi.app/blog/windowserver-high-cpu.md): WindowServer draws everything on your Mac's screens. Here's why it gets busy, what normal looks like, and the settings that actually calm it down.
- [Why is my Mac slow after a macOS update?](https://trybondi.app/blog/mac-slow-after-update.md): Mac slow after a macOS Sequoia or Tahoe update? It's re-indexing Spotlight, re-scanning photos and syncing iCloud. Here's what's running and how long it lasts.
- [Is Spotlight indexing slowing down your Mac?](https://trybondi.app/blog/spotlight-indexing-slow-mac.md): When mds_stores and mdworker are busy, Spotlight is rebuilding its index. Here's how to tell, how long it lasts, and how to keep folders out of it.
- [Bondi vs Activity Monitor: what each one is for](https://trybondi.app/blog/bondi-vs-activity-monitor.md): Looking for an Activity Monitor alternative for Mac? Activity Monitor shows every process; Bondi tells you what they mean. When to use which.
- [How Bondi's AI explains your Mac without making up a number](https://trybondi.app/blog/ai-that-never-makes-up-a-number.md): How Bondi's on-device AI, with Apple Intelligence where available, explains your Mac in one sentence while every figure stays measured and checked.
